NEW YORK (CNN) -- She survived a bloodbath at a Lane Bryant store in Tinley Park, Illinois, by playing dead. The only survivor, she gave police a detailed description of the gunman. The Illinois State police worked closely with the survivor to come up with a composite of the gunman. Police aren't identifying their witness to protect her safety. Five other women lost their lives at Lane Bryant on February 2, 2008. The gunman is still at large. The crime began to unfold shortly after 10 a.m. when a man posing as a delivery man walked into the store. He chatted briefly with two customers and two employees. Then, police said, he pulled out a gun and announced a holdup. He forced the four women into the back room, police said. He bound them with duct tape and placed them face down on the floor. Two more women who later entered the store also were taken to the back room, tied and placed next to the others.  Watch an update on the case » . Store manager Rhoda McFarland managed to call 911 from her cell phone at 10:44 a.m., just before she was shot to death. She got to her phone while the gunman was distracted, even though she was bound by the duct tape. On the call, posted on the Tinley Park police Web site, a man can be heard saying, "I'm losing it." The six women were shot execution style. Five of them were dead by the time police arrived, a few minutes after McFarland's call. A sixth woman survived. She, too, had been shot and left for dead, but tricked the killer by pretending to be dead. The killer was not wearing a mask or disguise, so she was able to describe him in detail. She told police he was a 6 foot African-American male, average weight, medium to dark skin tone, with braided hair and cornrows, husky build, and between 25 and 35 years old. His hair was pulled back, but one braid hung along his right cheek with light-green beads at the end of it, she told police. Police have released a composite sketch based on the witness' description. Besides store manager McFarland, the other women slain were Jennifer Bishop, Connie Woolfolk, Carrie Hudek Chiuso and Sarah Szafranski. The investigation remains open and active, and all theories are still being investigated, police say. The investigation has included a thorough vetting of the victims' backgrounds to determine whether any of them had any enemies. "None of the victimology so far has led to any suspects yet," said Commander Pat McCain of the Tinley Park Police Department. Police aren't ruling out any theories, including robbery. The gunman took a few hundred dollars, police said. "Certainly, the surviving witness didn't seem to recognize the killer, but maybe one of the dead victims knew him. We don't know," McCain said. The weapon used was a .40-caliber Glock. Bullet casings were left at the scene and the killer took the weapon with him. More than a year later, forensics from the crime scene are still being processed, police said. Investigators won't comment on whether the gunman left any fingerprints, hair or other trace evidence. Police say they have received more than 5,000 tips and feel this case will be solved. But at this point, they have not named a person of interest or a suspect. Investigators are asking for the public's help. There is a $100,000 reward for the arrest of the person or persons responsible for the Lane Bryant shootings. Have information? **TINLEY PARK, Ill.** — In one of the Chicago area’s most haunting unsolved mass murders, investigators say a surviving victim’s decision to remain motionless and pretend to be dead helped preserve her life — and later provided police with one of their most important clues: a composite sketch of the gunman.

The killings occurred on **Feb. 2, 2008**, inside a **Lane Bryant clothing store** in Tinley Park, a suburb southwest of Chicago. Five women were fatally shot during what authorities believe began as a robbery but escalated into a brutal execution-style attack.

The victims were identified as:

- **Jennifer Bishop**, 34  
- **Connie Woolfolk**, 37  
- **Carrie Hudek**, 22  
- **Rhoda McFarland**, 42  
- **Sarah Szafranski**, 22  

A sixth woman survived despite being shot. Police have said her account became central to the investigation.

### Gunman Entered Store Posing as a Customer

According to investigators, the attacker entered the Lane Bryant store in the morning and initially behaved like a customer. He later pulled a handgun and forced employees and shoppers toward the back of the store.

The women were bound and placed in a rear area of the business. Police have said the situation appeared to start as an armed robbery, but at some point the gunman opened fire on the victims.

The surviving witness was shot but remained conscious enough to realize that movement could draw the attacker’s attention. She **played dead**, lying still among the victims until the gunman left the store.

Her survival gave investigators a rare firsthand account of the suspect’s appearance, voice, behavior, and movements inside the store.

### Survivor Helped Create Composite Sketch

After the attack, the surviving witness worked with police artists to develop a **composite sketch** of the suspected gunman. The image depicted a Black male wearing a dark cap and coat, based on her recollection of the man who entered the store and carried out the attack.

Authorities also released a description of the suspect as a man roughly **5-foot-9 to 6 feet tall**, with a medium-to-stocky build. Police said he may have had braided hair or hair concealed beneath his cap, and he spoke in a calm but commanding manner during the crime.

The composite sketch was widely circulated in the Chicago area and nationally. Investigators hoped someone would recognize the man or recall suspicious behavior near the shopping center that morning.

### Witness Account Shaped the Timeline

The survivor’s testimony helped police reconstruct the sequence of events inside the store. Investigators learned that the gunman spent time in the shop before drawing his weapon, then directed the victims to the back.

Her account also helped authorities determine that the attacker likely fled shortly after the shootings. Despite an intensive search, no arrest was made.

Police reviewed surveillance footage from nearby businesses, followed tips, and examined possible links to other robberies. The case generated thousands of leads over the years, but none resulted in charges.

### Case Remains Unsolved

The Lane Bryant murders remain unsolved. Tinley Park police, the FBI, and other agencies have continued to seek information from the public.

Authorities have repeatedly emphasized that even a small detail could be significant — a person who came home acting strangely, someone who suddenly left the area, or an individual who resembled the sketch and had knowledge of the shopping center.

A reward has been offered at various points in the investigation for information leading to an arrest and conviction.

For the families of the victims, the surviving witness’s courage remains a crucial part of the case. By staying still and pretending to be dead, she survived an attack that killed five women — and her memory of the gunman gave investigators their clearest public lead in the search for the killer.

- Around **200 to 230 pounds**

- Wearing dark clothing at the time of the attack

Composite sketches released over the years depicted a man with a broad face and facial hair. Authorities have also said the suspect may have had braided hair or a distinctive hairstyle at the time, though appearances may have changed significantly since 2008.

Investigators have said the women were **bound** and shot in an execution-style attack in the rear of the store. The case has involved extensive forensic work, including analysis of physical evidence from the scene and the firearm evidence connected to the shootings.

Law enforcement agencies, including Tinley Park police and outside partners, have continued to treat the case as active. Over the years, rewards have been offered for information leading to an arrest and conviction.
